===Etymology 1===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*h₂eyḱ-}}
From {{der|en|enm|oun}}, {{m|enm|owen}}, from {{der|en|ang|āgen|t=own, proper, peculiar}}, originally the past participle of {{m|ang|āgan}}; from {{der|en|gmw-pro|*aigan|t=own}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*aiganaz|t=own}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*h₂eyḱ-|t=to have, possess}}. {{dbt|en|eigen-}}.
{{col-top|2|cog}}
Cognate with {{cog|sco|ain}}, {{m|sco|awin}}, {{m|sco|awn}}, {{m|sco|ayn|t=own}}, {{cog|stq|oain|t=own}}, {{cog|fy,nl,de|eigen|t=own}}, {{cog|da,nb,sv|egen|t=own}}, {{cog|fo|egin|t=own}}, {{cog|is|eigin}}, {{m|is|eiginn|t=own}}, {{cog|nn|eigen|t=own}}; also {{cog|os|исын|t=to take}}, {{cog|xto,txb|aik-|t=to know, recognize}}, {{cog|sa|ईश|t=owning, possessing}}. Originally past participle of the verb at hand in {{m+|en|owe}}.
{{col-bottom}}

====Alternative forms====
* {{alter|en|ain||Scotland}}
* {{alter|en|owne||obsolete}}

====Adjective====
{{en-adj|-}}

# {{senseid|en|belonging to}} [[belong|Belonging]] to; [[possess]]ed; [[acquire]]d and [[designate]]d by; [[proper]] to; [[property]] of; [[title]]d to; [[held]] in one's [[name]]; [[under]]/[[using]] the name of. {{n-g|Often marks a possessive determiner as reflexive, referring back to the subject of the clause or sentence.}}
#* {{RQ:King James Version|Deuteronomy|24|16|passage=The fathers shall not bee put to death for the children, neither shall the children be put to death for the fathers: euery man shall be put to death for his '''owne''' sinne.}}
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Tempest|IV|i|page=14|passage={{smallcaps|Prospero}}: Fairely ſpoke ; / Sit then, and talke with her, ſhe is thine '''owne''' ;}}
#* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=8|passage=I corralled the judge, and we started off across the fields, in no very mild state of fear of that gentleman's wife, whose vigilance was seldom relaxed. And thus we came by a circuitous route to Mohair, the judge occupied by his '''own''' guilty thoughts, and I by others not less disturbing.}}
#* {{RQ:Maxwell Mirror and the Lamp|chapter=10|passage=He looked round the poor room, at the distempered walls, and the bad engravings in meretricious frames, the crinkly paper and wax flowers on the chiffonier; and he thought of a room like Father Bryan's, with panelling, with cut glass, with tulips in silver pots, such a room as he had hoped to have for his '''own'''.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=2013-06-21|author=w:Oliver Burkeman
|volume=189|issue=2|page=27|magazine=w:The Guardian Weekly
|title=[http://www.guardian.co.uk/technology/2013/may/10/conscious-computing-twitter-facebook-google The tao of tech]
|passage=The dirty secret of the internet is that all this distraction and interruption is immensely profitable. Web companies like to boast about […], or offering services that let you{{...}} "share the things you love with the world" and so on. But the real way to build a successful online business is to be better than your rivals at undermining people's control of their '''own''' attention.}}
# Not [[share|shared]].
#: {{ux|en|When we move into the new house, the kids will each have their '''own''' bedroom.}}
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} [[peculiar|Peculiar]], [[domestic]].
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} Not [[foreign]].

=====Usage notes=====
* Often used for implication of ownership, often with emphasis. In modern usage, it always follows a possessive determiner, or a noun in the possessive case.

===Etymology 2===
{{wp}}
{{root|en|ine-pro|*h₂eyḱ-}}
A {{back-formation|en|owner|nocap=1}}. Compare {{cog|ang|āgnian}}, {{cog|nl|eigenen}}, {{cog|de|eignen}}, {{cog|sv|ägna}}.

====Verb====
{{en-verb}}

# {{senseid|en|owner}}{{lb|en|transitive}} To have [[rightful]] [[possession]] of ([[property]], [[goods]] or [[capital]]); to have [[legal]] [[title]] to; to acquire a [[property]] or [[asset]].
#: {{ux|en|I '''own''' this car.}}
# {{senseid|en|sovereignty}}{{lb|en|transitive}} To have recognized political sovereignty over a place, territory, as distinct from the ordinary connotation of property ownership.
#: {{ux|en|The United States '''owns''' Point Roberts by the terms of the Treaty of Oregon.}}
# {{senseid|en|overwhelm}}{{lb|en|transitive|informal}} To defeat or [[embarrass]]; to [[overwhelm]].
#: {{ux|en|I will '''own''' my enemies.}}
#: {{ux|en|If he wins, he will '''own''' you.}}
# {{senseid|en|enslave}}{{lb|en|transitive}} To virtually or figuratively [[enslave]].
# {{senseid|en|gaming}}{{lb|en|online gaming|slang}} To defeat, dominate, or be above.
#: {{syn|en|pwn}}
# {{senseid|en|pwned}}{{lb|en|transitive|computing|slang}} To [[illicit]]ly obtain [[administrator|administrative]] access to a [[computer system]], thereby having full access to all the [[file]]s thereon (including [[executable#Noun|executables]]).
#: {{syn|en|pwn|0wn}}
#* {{quote-newsgroup
|en
|title=Re: An unusual situation
|accessdate=2016-09-24
|author=The Happiest Dragon Alive!!
|passage="TH15 5Y5T3M 15 '''0WN3D'''"
|url=https://groups.google.com/forum/#!original/alt.sysadmin.recovery/IsdIZqfW_sM/9UTRiIoSy74J
|date=1996/06/21
|id=4qe8pc$8ti@nerd.apk.net
}}
# {{senseid|en|excel}}{{lb|en|intransitive|slang}} To be very good.
# {{senseid|en|admit}}{{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[admit]], [[concede]], [[grant]], [[allow]]; not to deny.
#* {{RQ:Melville Moby-Dick|passage=I '''own''' thy speechless, placeless power; but to the last gasp of my earthquake life will dispute its unconditional, unintegral mastery in me.}}
#* {{RQ:Conrad Heart of Darkness|part=I|passage=I am sorry to '''own''' I began to worry then.}}
#* {{RQ:Lawrence Sons and Lovers|passage=They learned how perfectly peaceful the home could be. And they almost regretted—though none of them would have '''owned''' to such callousness—that their father was soon coming back.|5}}
# {{senseid|en|acknowledge}}{{lb|en|transitive}} To [[acknowledge]].
#: {{ux|en|I must '''own''' that I have been at fault all this time.}}
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Tempest|v|text=Two of those fellows you must know and '''own'''.}}
#* {{RQ:Carlyle Past and Present|2|1, ''Jocelin of Brakelond''|text=It must be '''owned''', the good Jocelin, spite of his beautiful childlike character, is but an altogether imperfect 'mirror' of these old-world things!}}
# {{senseid|en|proudly acknowledge}}{{lb|en|transitive}} To [[proud]]ly [[acknowledge]]; to not be [[ashamed]] or [[embarrassed]] of.
# {{senseid|en|own up}}{{lb|en|transitive}} To take [[responsibility]] for.
#* {{RQ:NYT|en|title=As Political Violence Rises, Trump Condemns One Side|date=2025-09-11|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/09/11/us/politics/political-violence-trump-blame.html|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20251031213905/https://www.nytimes.com/2025/09/11/us/politics/political-violence-trump-blame.html|author=Luke Broadwater; Alan Feuer|quotee=w:Nancy Mace|passage=Representative Nancy Mace, Republican of South Carolina, told reporters that Democrats “'''own'''” the assassination of Mr. Kirk. When a reporter questioned her about attacks on Democrats, she cut him off. “Democrats '''own''' this,” she said. “We’re talking about Charlie Kirk right now.”}}
# {{senseid|en|recognise}}{{lb|en|transitive}} To [[recognise]].
#: {{ux|en|I '''own''' him as a son of my own.}}
# {{senseid|en|claim}}{{lb|en|transitive}} To [[claim]] as one's own.
# {{senseid|en|confess}}{{lb|en|intransitive|UK|_|dialectal}} To [[confess]].
